title: Native Windows lab provisioning
summary: The native Windows lab adapter uses Windows OpenSSH and PowerShell, an interactive scheduled task for desktop screenshots and console checks, profile goldens that preserve live identities, and a lease-bound machine-settings recovery journal. Standard-user task control uses native Task Scheduler COM; protected SYSTEM receipts provide current-lease Windows feature evidence. SSH is key-only from any address. Human RDP is allowed over verified Tailscale self addresses or adapters, never the public internet; an SSH forward remains available for bootstrap. A private bounded SYSTEM probe verifies tailnet identity without selecting an administrator's Tailscale profile. Fresh setup teaches localhost SSH/RDP password custody and Start > Tailscale > Get Started with the existing account and expected-device approval. Provisioning privately backs up and disables only the verified vendor tray shortcut, refusing unexpected or renamed startup entries. SYSTEM probe receipts retain exact allowlisted failures and replace unknown errors with a fixed safe reason. Acceptance requires two separate cold boots with completed automatic standard-user logon, unchanged tailnet identity and startup key, private routes, and no tray autostart or intervening profile repair; command success alone does not prove persistence. Harness desktop and CLI sign-ins require separate visible-app and real-request proof before goldens. Provisioning and live restoration require separate machine receipts before readiness is claimed. A macOS controller installs a controllable Windows App before a bounded VM window; local installation authentication and a timed private RDP password prompt are operator handoffs. Administrator staging cleanup failures remain fatal with named recovery and retain completed command diagnostics privately; they do not prove the primary command failed. Native vendor PowerShell installers decode raw UTF-8 response bytes consistently for binary and text media types.
